data.name: Sword Master VR
data.detailed_description:
Sword Master VR, now with support for Oculus Touch & HTC Vive, brings you intense sword fighting gameplay that has never been possible in traditional video games. Taking full advantage of room-scale virtual reality, you must learn to fight with realistic swords in full 360 combat! React quickly, duck and dodge, deflect incoming attacks! Sword Master VR is not a game of standing still and lightly wiggling your sword in the enemies face. Sword Master VR is a game of endurance, skill, speed, and most importantly, to become a master of the blade.

NEW!
10 Unlockable Shields! Each level that you beat in Expert mode unlocks a new shield!

Features:
  • Intense & Challenging Sword Fighting!
  • 8 Unlockable Swords!
  • 7 Enemy Variations!
  • 10 Challenge Levels (Including a Boss Level!)
  • 4 Difficulty Modes (1 Unlockable mode!)

Safety Notice:
Sword Master VR requires players to swing their controllers in virtual reality. Play at your own risk. Eric Tereshinski, the game's developer, is not responsible for any destruction of property or the injury of yourself or anyone else while playing Sword Master VR.
Please play far away from your TV, have plenty of space, use high quality wrist straps, remove all children from the room, DO NOT play near any stairs, and enjoy the game :)

Room-Scale Info:
Sword Master VR will play correctly with as little as 2m x 1.5m playspace. However, it is recommended for best playing experience to have 2.5m x 2.5m of playspace or more.

Oculus Setup Info:
This game requires the use of motion controllers and roomscale. If you have the basic Oculus Touch kit with two sensors, two controllers, and your Oculus HMD, you can set up your playspace for roomscale and play Sword Master VR. To set up roomscale, you must set up your two sensors in opposite corners if the room. Adding a third sensor may improve your experience, but two sensors still works quite well.

data.short_description: Enter the virtual reality sword fighting arena of Sword Master VR! Test your skills with the blade against smart and interactive AI enemies! Unlock new swords and game modes! Prove that you are the sword master!

reviews.review:
As someone who regularly trains with swords in real life, there is a near infinite amount of things I could say about this game. I'll try to get it down into a simple pros / cons list with a bit more detail.

PROS:

*The cutting and blocking feels absolutely amazing. You can almost feel the weight when you parry or land a proper strike.

*The armor system on the enemies makes every fight challenging and unique. You can only attack an enemy where he has no armor, something very rarely seen in games.

*The developer seriously listens to good suggestions. Just in the couple of days I've been talking with him about some realistic facets of sword combat, the game has become a LOT more balanced, and hopefully it will continue to improve.

*Has a low graphics mode that enables the game to run on really bad PCs. I have a single 660ti and with low graphics on, it runs flawlessly. One of maybe four games that I can currently run at full FPS in VR.

*Simple. This may sound like a con, but not in this game. It is a PURE, unclogged swordfighting game. No nonsense. Pick up a blade and fight. There are other games like Raw Data and Spell Fighter that feature sword combat, but this is the only one where that is the entire focus of the whole game, and therefor can be made far greater than any other.

*Complex. Yes, I'm just doing this to mess with you now. Just kidding, but this game has so many nuances to succeeding that a seemingly simple game can be made very complicated. The different sized blades sacrifice realism for balance, which while unintuitive, is completely needed to keep things fair. Example: The greatsword has a six-foot reach, deals two damage. Combat knife has only the reach of your arm, deals six damage. And there are blades of every size in between, all with their own stats. Some are far better at thrusting, some at slashing, some have an edge on each side and can be used in powerful combination attacks.

*Music sounds a lot like the Japanese Godzilla theme, which is a pro in any situation.

Alright, now for the unfortunate and hopefully soon to be fixed CONS:

1: Animations are terrible. I'm sorry, there's no other way to say this. Especially in the defensive circle-walk the enemies do, they're holding their swords through their own chests. I would suggest changing the animation for that walk to something like what is seen here: http://i.imgur.com/XTvLMM9.jpg - With the sword held in front of the shield, ready to lash out while still keeping defenses up.

2: Complete lack of sword physics VS the enemy. I understand that this may be a matter of opinion, but it is my belief that if I strike an enemy, without enough power to deal damage, the sword should slide along the targets body, weapon, or shield instead of just phasing through them. It would be a lot easier to tell if I'm just hitting too lightly or missing completely if the swords had actual physical rigging as seen in Raw Data or the guns in H3VR.

3: Give us an option for an off-hand shield :-D

And a final suggestion, unlockable skins for weapons. Only once all the big issues are ironed-out, of course. I'd love to see a medieval dagger skin for the combat knife, a Zweihander skin for the greatsword, perhaps a copyright-friendly lightsword skin for the katana? All up to the developer. If only I knew how to create this stuff, I'd make a skin unlockable for every level beaten and give them all to Eric.

Anyway, that's the end of my review. With the very few downsides, buying this game is a resounding "MUST." It is by far the best melee combat game released for VR at this time, and with continuous improvements and expansions, that title could last a very long time. Master Indie has a monopoly on this right now, and I deeply hope to see him take full advantage of this.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7
  • Processador: i5
  • Memória: 6 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: GTX 770 or AMD R9 390
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 550 MB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR. Room Scale 2m by 1.5m area required
  • Notas adicionais: HTC Vive OR Oculus Rift with Touch in room-scale configuration
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo: Windows 10
  • Processador: i7
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: GTX 970
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 550 MB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: HTC Vive OR Oculus Rift with Touch in room-scale configuration & 3rd sensor
